newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's sees better Nov trade gap vs Oct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's sees better Nov trade gap vs Oct.

text.p: Brazil's Ministry of Industry and Commerce expects a lower trade deficit in November than October's record $1.3 billion gap, said Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade.
"We can expect a significantly more satisfactory result in November than in October," Cortes told reporters after announcing total November exports of $3.912 billion.
Cortes said the ministry did not yet know what the level of imports was in November because the figures must be calculated manually.
"Whatever, we expect that the deficit in November will be effectively lower,... confirming the possibility that the peak of imports for this year may have been registered in October," he said.
Cortes said average daily exports in November rose to $195.6 million, with 20 working days, from $190.4 million over 22 working days in October.
He said the main contributor to the better result was a rise in exports of manufactured goods, where the daily average of overseas sales was 6.02 percent higher at $109.3 million than in October.
Exports of primary commodities were also strong, registering a record for the month of November of $982 million.
